simple.meaning: מוֹרָט (môwrâṭ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “obstinate , i.e. independent.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 18:2. The surrounding contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מוֹרָט (H4178) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מוֹרָט (môwrâṭ) / H4178 is traced through Isaiah 18:2, Isaiah 18:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: that sends ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus on the waters, saying, “Go, you swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide!”

In that time, a present will be brought to Yahweh of Armies from a people tall and smooth, even from a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of Yahweh of Armies, Mount Zion.
